name: Finerenone
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Finerenone is a nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (MRA). The US label sets the starting dose by estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and serum potassium, and does not recommend starting it below eGFR 25 mL/min/1.73 m2.

bands.recommendation: Start 20 mg once daily (label). Do not start if serum potassium >5.0 mEq/L. CKD with diabetes: target 20 mg. Heart failure (LVEF ≥40%): target 40 mg.

Start 10 mg once daily (label: eGFR ≥25 to <60). CKD with diabetes: recheck potassium at 4 weeks; increase to 20 mg if K ≤4.8 mEq/L and eGFR has not fallen >30%. Heart failure: target 20 mg; uptitrate if K <5.0 mEq/L (label Table 3).
eGFR 25–29: start 10 mg once daily as above. eGFR <25: initiation not recommended (label).
Initiation not recommended (label: eGFR <25). Label silent on continuing if eGFR falls below 25 during treatment; continue only with close potassium monitoring and specialist input.

hd.text: No data in label. Insufficient data: avoid or use with specialist input.

pd.text: No data in label. Insufficient data: avoid or use with specialist input.

crrt.text: No data in label. Insufficient data: avoid.

dialyzable: Unlikely to be removed by hemodialysis (about 90% protein bound; label).
monitoring: Serum potassium and eGFR before starting, 4 weeks after starting or changing dose, and periodically. CKD with diabetes: withhold if K >5.5 mEq/L; restart at 10 mg when K ≤5.0 mEq/L. Heart failure: uptitrate if K <5.0; K 5.5 to <6.0 reduce one step (withhold if on 10 mg); K ≥6.0 withhold; restart at 10 mg when K <5.5 (label Table 3).

pediatric.approved_ages: Safety and efficacy not established below 18 years (label).
pediatric.egfr_equation: Bedside Schwartz: eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m2) = 0.413 x height (cm) / serum creatinine (mg/dL)
